notes.why: Each track's notes become notes; the track's Volume (0–127, holding until the next) is the velocity, 127 where a track has none (Pedal M1's default).

remarks: Neo Sampler plays every track's note: Pedal M1, as profiled, played one voice of a chord (its multi-track note workaround), so chords sound fuller after the move.
Pedal M1 mixes a stereo wave to mono; Neo Sampler keeps it stereo (uncorrelated channels read about 3 dB louder).
Pedal M1 reads a wave's first layer and caches it; Neo Sampler picks a layer by its root and follows the wavetable as it changes.

ReBuzz holds a wave parameter at 1 or more, so Pedal M1's zones 2–4 always play (wave 1 at its defaults, from Buzz C-4, C-5 and C-6 up): the conversion keeps them as zones 2–4, the same wave, so it sounds the same.

Its LFOs and portamento have no counterpart (listed as unmapped); Pedal M1's resonance is a 2-pole SVF's (Q 0.5 to 4), Neo Sampler's LP 12 a ladder's 2-pole output, the same at 0 % and near it in peak height above (it passes more above the cutoff).

tolerance.measured: Linux (tools/headless-replace.py, and by hand), a line of four notes (A3 at the wave's root, A4, E3, A2) from a saw (A3) and a square (A4) in the song's wavetable: at its defaults −0.2 dB, bands within 0.2 dB; a key zone (the square from F#3) and both oscillators (OSC2 an octave up at half level) −0.1 dB, within 0.1 dB; its envelopes and filter (attack, sustain, release, cutoff 2.5 kHz with its envelope) −0.5 dB, within 0.7 dB; key tracking 100 % at 1 kHz −0.2 dB, within 0.2 dB; the track Volume at 64 −0.1 dB, within 0.2 dB. Per note the third octaves agree within 0.3 dB to 6 kHz
tolerance.why_not: Not within: resonance (25 %: −1.9 dB, 3.2 dB at the cutoff; 50 %: −2.4 dB, 4.5 dB at 3.15 kHz): Neo Sampler's LP 12 is a ladder's 2-pole output, whose resonance takes away bass and passes more above the cutoff than Pedal M1's SVF. Its LFOs and portamento have no counterpart. A wave pitched an octave down is brighter on Neo Sampler (+2.4 dB at 10 kHz: Pedal M1's cubic interpolation dulls it), and one pitched up loses Pedal M1's aliases (above 12 kHz here).
